chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man who prayed without taharah, or forgot prayers and did not perform them, or slept through them, so he said:

He should make it up when he remembers it, at whatever hour he remembers it, whether by night or by day. Then when the time of a salat enters and he has not completed what he had missed, he should make up prayers so long as he does not fear that the time of this salat which has arrived will pass; and this one has more right to its time, so he should perform it. Then when he has completed it, he should perform what he had missed from what had passed, and he should not perform even a single rak'ah of supererogatory prayer until he completes the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِوَقْتِهَا: more entitled to its time, meaning the present obligatory prayer has priority within its own time
key_terms.ذَكَرَهَا: he remembered it, referring to recollection of the missed prayer
key_terms.فَاتَهُ: it escaped him, meaning the prayer he missed
key_terms.وَقْتُ صَلَاةٍ: the time of a salat, meaning the appointed time of the current obligatory prayer
key_terms.يَتَطَوَّعْ: he performs a supererogatory act of prayer
key_terms.يَقْضِيهَا: he makes it up, meaning he performs the missed salat as qada'

ai.seo_question: When should missed salat be made up, and does the current prayer time take priority?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the ruling for making up missed salat, whether missed through forgetfulness, sleep, or lack of taharah. It states that missed prayers are to be performed upon remembrance at any time, but if the current prayer time is at risk of expiring, the present prayer takes priority, and supererogatory prayer should be left until the obligatory missed prayer is made up.
